opportunities.title: [BUG] Project-scope native plugin: Claude Code's first session loads the plugin's MCP server but not its skills or hooks
opportunities.excerpt:
Reporting and investigating a bug need no permission. Before implementing a
substantive fix for inclusion in APM, obtain human scope approval and a review
contact on this issue. Trivial documentation corrections have standing
preapproval. See [Contributing](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

For vulnerabilities, use [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/SECURITY.md)
instead of a public issue. Remove credentials and other sensitive data from logs.

**Describe the bug**
`apm install` at project scope deploys a Claude-format plugin to `.agents/plugins/<plugin>/` and declares it in `.claude/settings.json` with a **relative** marketplace path (`"path": "./.agents/plugins"`). In the first Claude Code session on a machine where Claude has not seen that marketplace yet (any CI run, `claude -p`, claude-code-action, a fresh clone), Claude loads the plugin and starts its MCP server. It does not load the plugin's skills, and the plugin's `SessionStart` hook does not fire. The second session in the same `HOME` loads everything.

Claude's own native install writes the same settings except for the path. `claude plugin marketplace add ./.agents/plugins --scope project` followed by `claude plugin install <plugin>@<marketplace> --scope project` writes an **absolute** path, and that loads fully in a first session.

The skills go missing with no error from either tool. This is the symptom reported in #4995 for `claude -p` and claude-code-action.

**To Reproduce**
Cell id `claude-headless-project` of the real-harness probe (`scripts/real_harness/probe.py` on branch `danielmeppiel-ql-real-harness-lane`). Same result in `claude-normal-project` (interactive TUI) and `claude-worktree-project`.
1. Fresh `HOME`, with the folder trusted in `~/.claude.json` (`projects[<abs path>].hasTrustDialogAccepted: true`).
2. A plugin with `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `skills/rh-probe-skill/SKILL.md`, `hooks/hooks.json` (a `SessionStart` hook that appends to a marker file) and `.mcp.json` (a stdio server).
3. In a git repository: `apm.yml` with `targets: [claude]` and that plugin as a local dependency, then `apm install`.
4. `claude -p "hi" --output-format stream-json --verbose`, then read the `system/init` event.

Result (Claude Code 2.1.323 and 2.1.326, apm at `main` 837562cd86c):

| Variant (same plugin bytes) | Plugin in init `plugins` | MCP handsh

opportunities.title: security(mcp): memory_freeze_run reads any file path the process can open
opportunities.excerpt:
**Severity:** high · **Control:** MCP · **Source:** muse-security audit (2026-11-23)

## Evidence
`src/snapshot.ts:123-130`:
```ts
let task = options.task;
if (existsSync(task)) { task = readFileSync(task, "utf-8").trim(); }
```
reachable from `src/mcp.ts:2780-2787`, where `task` is the raw tool argument. `{"task":"/home/user/.ssh/id_rsa"}` is a valid call on the default tool surface; the content is also written into `.memory/runs/<id>/snapshot.json`, which `memory_freeze_list` serves later.

## Impact
An LLM steered by prompt injection — or any unauthenticated HTTP client (see the auth issue) — turns a benign "freeze this run" tool into an arbitrary-file-read primitive covering SSH keys, `.env` and cloud credentials. The content lands in model context and in a persisted snapshot.

## Fix
Treat `task` as data only: drop the `existsSync`/`readFileSync` branch, or add a separate `task_file` argument validated with `resolveWithin(workspaceRoot, …)` plus a size cap. Redact through `redactSecrets` before it enters the snapshot.

## Unblock
`memory_freeze_run({task:"/etc/passwd"})` must not return the file's contents.

opportunities.title: security(mcp): HTTP transport fails open when no token is configured
opportunities.excerpt:
**Severity:** high · **Control:** MCP · **Source:** muse-security audit (2026-11-23)

## Evidence
`src/mcp.ts:3784-3787`:
```ts
const isAuthRequired = options.requireAuth || validTokens.size > 0;
if (!isAuthRequired) return { authenticated: true };
```
`src/cli/ecosystem.ts:560-583` takes `--host`/`--port` from flags while `--token` is optional, and only passes `allowedOrigins`/`allowedHosts` when flagged.

## Impact
`memory serve --host 0.0.0.0` — a documented way to let containers connect — exposes every tool unauthenticated, including `memory_delete` with `confirm:true`. The loopback default remains reachable via DNS rebinding because host/origin validation is off by default.

## Fix
Require a token (or an explicit `--insecure`) whenever `host` is not loopback, and refuse to start otherwise. Always populate `allowedHosts`/`allowedOrigins` from the bind address when unspecified.

## Unblock
Starting with a non-loopback host and no token either fails at startup or rejects requests with 401.

opportunities.title: Security: bump Node base image and dependencies in backend and mcp-server (multer, nodemailer, body-parser, ...)
opportunities.excerpt:
Found by a scheduled Trivy scan (v0.76.2, DB of 2026-11-23) of the published `backend` and `mcp-server` images. Risk is rated by whether the code actually reaches the vulnerable path.

## Risk: MEDIUM — worth doing soon

| Package | Image | Fixed in | Why it matters here |
|---|---|---|---|
| multer 1.4.5-lts.1 (via `@nestjs/platform-express` 11.0.1) | backend | 2.3.0 | 10 denial-of-service advisories on multipart parsing. Used by `POST /scraper/import/upload` and the plugin upload. Both are behind `JwtAuthGuard`, so only a logged-in user can trigger them. Fix: bump `@nestjs/platform-express` to a current 11.x. |
| nodemailer 8.0.1 | backend | 8.0.8 (9.x/10.x for all) | CVE-2026-82662 TLS certificate verification disabled in some paths (info disclosure of SMTP traffic); addressparser ReDoS. Used in `push.service.ts`. |
| body-parser 1.20.3 / 2.2.1 | both | 1.20.9 / 2.4.0 | CVE-2026-111181 DoS via decompression stream error, reachable before auth on any JSON endpoint that accepts a compressed body. |
| hono 4.11.4, @hono/node-server 1.19.9 (via `@modelcontextprotocol/node`) | mcp-server | 4.12.25 / 1.19.10 | serveStatic file access and CORS origin reflection. Low unless serveStatic or hono's CORS middleware is used; bump with the MCP packages anyway. |
| joi 18.0.2 | backend | 18.3.1 | ReDoS in email / isoDate validation if user input goes through those rules. |
| adm-zip 0.5.16 | backend | 0.6.1 | DoS / zip-bomb and permission bits on extract. Admin-only plugin upload; path traversal is already guarded. |

## Risk: LOW — not reachable in practice, cleared by the same rebuild

| Package | Fixed in | Why low |
|---|---|---|
| **proxy-addr 2.0.7** (critical, CVE-2026-90711) | 2.0.8 | Only matters with `trust proxy` set to subnets; neither app sets `trust proxy`. |
| **OpenSSL 3.5.5** (critical, CVE-2026-31789) | 3.5.6+ | Heap overflow on 32-bit systems only; plus 6 high (DoS, one use-after-free in CMS/PKCS7). Cleared by a newer `node:24-alpine` base. |
| **tar 7.5.1** (critical, CVE-2026-59873) + pacote, sigstore, glob, minimatch, brace-expansion | — | Inside npm's own bundled copy in the base image; npm is not run at runtime. |
| mysql2, hono, effect, defu, deepmerge-ts, lodash | — | Pulled in by prisma / build tooling; not used at runtime with PostgreSQL. |
| path-to-regexp 8.2.0 | 8.4.0 | ReDoS only with crafted *route definitions*, which are ours. |

## Fix

inboundFeedback.title: [Agent trial] Maintainer assignment: preserve SIGINT child exit status in cage relay
inboundFeedback.body:
Maintainer-assigned real engineering task for the resident. This is not external adoption feedback.

Observed on the current source: src/cage/relay.js exits with 143 when its child terminates with SIGINT. The relay's stated contract is to leave with the child's exit status; the conventional shell status for SIGINT is 128 + 2 = 130.

Reproduction (run from the repository, Node on Linux/macOS):

```js
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, [
  'src/cage/relay.js', '/tmp/unused-agenthub-task.sock', '0', '--',
  process.execPath, '-e', "process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGINT')"
], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5000 });
console.log(result.status); // observed 143; expected 130
```

The unused Unix socket is never contacted by this reproduction. Port 0 requests an ephemeral loopback port. No external service or credentials are needed.

Acceptance:
- Independently reproduce the baseline failure with a new regression test.
- Correct source behavior without editing existing tests, the controller, workflows or manifests.
- Preserve ordinary numeric child exit codes, SIGTERM=143 and SIGKILL=137.
- The exact regression must fail before the change and pass after it; the complete existing suite must pass.
- Save a candidate branch/PR with actual execution evidence. Do not claim success from a proposed patch or model review.

Start with src/cage/relay.js. Do not pursue the earlier unverified port-binding-race hypothesis for this task. If blocked, record the actual tool error and checkpoint.

This task tests one useful repair, not autonomous general intelligence or adoption.
